messages.content:
Work out the ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis category for the episode below. The principal diagnosis is the single condition established after investigation to be chiefly responsible for the patient's episode of admitted care. It is not the patient's most serious comorbidity, not the presenting symptom, and not the procedure performed.

Think in three steps: first name the condition chiefly responsible for the admission, second name the ICD-10-AM chapter letter it belongs to, third give the three-character category.

Example 1
Hospital course: A 72-year-old man with a 50 pack-year smoking history was admitted with three days of worsening breathlessness and purulent sputum. Spirometry showed an FEV1/FVC ratio of 0.52. He was treated with nebulised bronchodilators, oral prednisolone and antibiotics for an infective exacerbation of his long-standing airflow limitation.
Answer: Irreversible airflow limitation in a heavy smoker with an infective exacerbation is chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, chapter J, category J44.
CODE: J44

Example 2
Hospital course: A 58-year-old man presented with crushing central chest pain radiating to the jaw. The electrocardiogram showed ST elevation in the anterior leads and high-sensitivity troponin rose from 40 to 2100 ng/L. He underwent primary percutaneous coronary intervention with a stent to the proximal left anterior descending artery.
Answer: ST elevation with a rising troponin and culprit-vessel stenting is an acute myocardial infarction, chapter I, category I21.
CODE: I21

Hospital course:
Discharge Summary:

Patient Name: N/A
Age: 24
Gender: Female
Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Hospital Course:
The patient was admitted to our hospital with acute pulmonary edema due to severe aortic valve insufficiency. She had previously been diagnosed with Takayasu's disease and had undergone multiple surgeries, including replacement of the distal ascending aorta and hemiarch, stenosis of celiac artery and superior mesenteric artery, and stenosis of the orifices of both renal arteries. She had a graft used to direct blood flow from the right internal iliac artery to all stenosed arteries. She also underwent a right nephrectomy due to acute thrombosis of the right renal artery graft. The patient was on steroid treatment since the diagnosis of her disease.

Treatment:
The patient underwent surgery to address the aortic valve insufficiency. The procedure was performed through a median sternotomy, and a composite graft with a mechanical valve was implanted. The patient's postoperative course was uneventful, and she was discharged from the hospital on the 10th postoperative day.

Follow-up:
The patient had a one year clinical follow-up that showed normal echocardiographical results, and she was doing well in normal daily activities.

Pathology:
Part of the dilated aortic root wall was sent for histological examination, which verified the diagnosis of Takayasu's arteritis.

Note:
The patient's condition was complex and required surgery to address the aortic valve insufficiency. The patient's postoperative course was uneventful, and she had a good one year clinical follow-up.

Write your reasoning in at most three short sentences, then a final line of exactly 'CODE: <letter><digit><digit>'.

text:
The condition chiefly responsible for this admission is severe aortic valve insufficiency, which caused the acute pulmonary oedema and was corrected with a composite mechanical valved graft. It is coded as non-rheumatic aortic valve disease in chapter I, category I35, with Takayasu's arteritis (M31.4) as the underlying cause. Coding Takayasu's as principal is arguable because the regurgitation came from root dilatation, but the episode centred on the valve.

CODE: I35
